stories.body:
OpenAI shipped ChatGPT Images 2.6 on Wednesday evening. The update adds animated GIFs, so a prompt or a still image can become a loop with adjustable speed and frame by frame edits. It also lets people save reference images of themselves, pets or characters and reuse them without uploading again. It is live today in ChatGPT and Codex across all tiers on web, desktop and mobile.

For developers, OpenAI released two new API image models, GPT Image 2.6 Flare and Sunburst. @OpenAI said Flare can return an image in as little as six seconds and the pair runs about 50% faster than before, while Sunburst targets higher quality and steadier consistency across edits. Image markup and SVG export ship alongside. The main @OpenAI post passed 294K views, and builders like @jerrod_lew were sharing GIF tests within minutes.

Why it matters: image generation is turning from a novelty into a workflow, and speed plus reusable references is what product teams need to put it inside apps. Watch API pricing for Flare and Sunburst, how Google and Midjourney answer on GIFs and consistency, and whether reference images raise new likeness and consent questions.

stories.headline: BAAI and Chinese lab partners introduce CausGround, a plug and play causal grounding layer for embodied planners
stories.summary: The Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence, with ECNU, NPU, UCAS and CASIA, introduced CausGround, a plug and play causal interaction grounding framework for embodied planners. @BAAIBeijing said it doubles embodied planning performance with zero parameter updates, targeting t
stories.body:
The Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence, with ECNU, NPU, UCAS and CASIA, introduced CausGround, a plug and play causal interaction grounding framework for embodied planners. @BAAIBeijing said it doubles embodied planning performance with zero parameter updates, targeting the latency and black box limits of end to end models like Astra.

The idea: planners that store experience as loose text or raw trajectories cannot separate true causal dependencies from scene clutter. CausGround reasons over causal structure while a frozen multimodal model only turns language into a goal state. BAAI reported gains over vanilla planners, SelfReVision and LookPlanGraph in simulated households and real dual arm manipulation, across six open weight backbones including Qwen3.5 and InternVL3.5.

Why it matters: if causal knowledge distilled in simulation can guide real robots without retraining, planners get better without new training runs. Watch for code release and independent replication.

stories.body:
A KAIST team released DreamFree, an imagination free World Action Model that controls robots without generating future video, while still getting better with stronger video models and more video data. It runs at 11 Hz on a single H200 with a 14B video diffusion backbone, which @Jaehyeong_Jo said is 17.8x faster than DreamZero.

The thread reports 64% average success on 10 real world DROID tasks versus 56% for DreamZero and 16% for pi0.5, and RoboCasa Kitchen success rising from 58.5% at 5B to 71.7% at 14B. Earlier imagination free models like Fast WAM did not improve when scaled from 5B to 14B, which is the gap DreamFree targets. A project page, code and arXiv paper are out, and co author @SeonghyeonYe amplified the release.

Why it matters: world models promise robots that learn from video, but generating futures is slow. DreamFree keeps the video prior and drops the latency. Watch for replication on other robot platforms.
